properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's words, 2026-10-29:

"There is a lot of work right now of using super models (not released to public) to complete some mathematical proofs. As is the whole philosophy of flo2 ecosystem, I have a philosophy (maybe a line of reasoning) that human + ai agent + reflow2 can potentially solve these without ultra powerful ai models. In essence, my thought is that super powerful models are needed because laying out these proofs inside the model is complex, but if the complex structure can be "written down" (as in use reflow2 as your notes/sketchpad), then the agent no longer has to keep the complex mathematical proofs all within its context, but can focus on the "holes" in the proof. Then explore them, test them, and "write" them down. It can also iterate through trial and error and again, can write this down continue trying to solve something. ... This allows the AI to be good at what it is good at, allows reflow2 to be good at what it is good at, and the human gets a nice end-to-end, documented proof."

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) RECORD THE THESIS AS A LINE OF REASONING in a design of its own (design-an-argument): its premises (a model's difficulty with long proofs is partly holding the structure; a written-down structure removes that load; the remaining work is local to each hole), its conclusion, and the objections below as statements, so the thesis itself can be refuted or supported by what the trials show.
(b) TEST IT BY MEASUREMENT before believing it: the same model on the same problem, once with reflow2 as its notes and once without, on problems whose answers are known, so a difference can be seen and counted.
(c) TAKE IT AS A WORKING BELIEF and go straight to attempts on the open problems.

PUSHBACK (recorded beside the idea, not against it):
- Holding the structure is not obviously the hard part of the famous open problems. People have had paper, unlimited notes and decades, and the Riemann Hypothesis and Navier–Stokes stayed open; what is missing there is the idea that closes the hole, not the bookkeeping around it. The thesis is strongest where bookkeeping IS the burden: long proofs with many cases, recovering after a lost context, and checking a proof someone else wrote.
- Written-down notes do not make a model better at the one step that is hard; they make every other step cheaper and visible. That may still be decisive for some problems, which is why (b) is the honest test.
- A frontier-model claim can itself be disputed: the Navier–Stokes map (design ad65e4983833f39f) records a claimed result whose formal statement's faithfulness is contested. An end-to-end record helps exactly there: it is what lets a person scrutinise a claim, which is the part of the thesis least in doubt.

COST (a finding): (a) small, one design; (b) moderate, bounded, and the only option that can show the thesis wrong; (c) unbounded.
properties.name: OPEN — can a person, an ordinary agent and reflow2 together close holes in an unfinished proof, the work today attempted with unreleased frontier models, because the proof's structure is written down and the agent only has to hold the hole it is working on?
properties.rationale:
Anthony, thinking out loud after the proof ladder (primes to Navier–Stokes) left the Riemann and Navier–Stokes designs as maps with their holes recorded. It is his statement of the flo2 philosophy applied to open mathematics. Accepted intent already holds that a design can BE a proof (req:a-design-can-be-a-proof) and that the agent proposes speculative links that only the person accepts (dec:idea-speculate-the-bridge-that-would-close-a-gap-then-test-it); what is open is whether this setup can CLOSE a hole, not whether it can record one.
